data.title: PLI scheme to help telecom firms stay competitive amid US tariffs: Scindia
data.description:
Indian manufacturers, particularly telecom equipment makers, were globally competitive and would remain so on the back of the production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme, even amid proposed US tariffs, said Telecom Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia.
 
"Our PLI scheme has done extremely well, over 100,000 crores in sales, over close to 36,000 crores in exports and I think India has always been competitive and will continue to remain competitive," the minister said, speaking on the sidelines of a briefing on the Department of Posts on Thursday.
 
His remarks came a day after the US proposed a fresh round of tariffs of up to 25 per cent on Indian goods, although the proposed rate could be lowered to 17 per cent if India and the US reach a trade agreement.
  
Under the PLI scheme for telecom and network equipment, India has exported just about $1 billion worth of telecom products, accounting for 0.23 per cent of India's overall exports as of 2024, according to data from Niti Aayog. Imports remained high at $3.6 billion.
 
Telecom equipment makers said they were in a wait-and-watch mode as the final tariffs were yet to be decided, and some products, such as smartphones and routers, remained outside the purview of the tariffs.
 
According to some executives, exports of optical fibre, optical fibre cables, base stations, antennas, customer premises equipment, and components to the US were limited and would remain at existing levels until January.
 
"While its too early to say anything with certainty, the existing tariffs will continue to hold till the new ones get notified," said an executive from the industry body representing telecom equipment manufacturers in India.
 
"We're evaluating this, although these tariffs are currently as a proposal level," said another executive from a leading telecom equipment maker who did not want to be identified.
 
Rohan Lobo, partner and industry leader – technology, media and telecommunications, Deloitte South Asia, said that the impact was likely to be uneven since smartphones accounted for a large component of India's telecom-related exports and were outside the purview of both the additional US duty currently in force and the higher tariff proposed on November 25, 2026.
 
"Exposure is likely to be in a small but growing segment primarily in optical fiber and cable, base stations, antennas, and components. There are three factors that are likely to shape the outcome. Firstly, the final scope of product exemptions is still open to consultation. Secondly, the progress of the India–US trade agreement and the possibility of negotiated rate. Thirdly, India's position relative to other competing manufacturing locations like Thailand and Malaysia where the rate proposed is 18 per cent," Lobo said.
 
India has disputed the United States Trade Representative's (USTR's) findings on structural excess capacity and reiterated its commitment to ongoing bilateral trade negotiations.
 
Lobo noted that routers were exempt from the proposed tariff, but there had been barriers to importing foreign-made consumer routers since March 2026. "Similarly, AI data-center demand has left US fiber in short supply and buyers may not have a choice but to absorb the duty," he added.

data.title: Cabinet clears fresh women's reservation Bill with 50% seat rise formula
data.description:
The Union Cabinet on Friday approved a fresh delimitation-linked women's reservation Constitution Amendment Bill. While copies of the Bill were yet to be circulated among lawmakers, government sources asserted that the fresh Bill hard-coded in its text a uniform 50 per cent rise in Lok Sabha seats for all states. The formula, they said, would assuage the concerns of the southern states and help pave the way for its passage in the special session of Parliament next week.
 
In April, the government had insisted that no state’s share of seats in the Lok Sabha would decline, but did not include any such guarantee in the text of the Bill. The Bill fell 54 votes short of the two-thirds mark, which is required for the passage of a constitutional amendment. But the arithmetic has changed since that defeat nearly eight months ago.
 
 
The split in the Trinamool Congress led to 20 of its Lok Sabha MPs joining the fledgling Nationalist Citizens Party of India, which is now a constituent of the National Democratic Alliance (NDA). Six of the Shiv Sena (UBT)’s MPs joined the Shiv Sena, and the return of the Shiromani Akali Dal, which has one Lok Sabha MP, to the NDA has increased the NDA’s numbers.
 
There were indications on Friday evening that the government's proposal of a 50 per cent increase in seats for all states based on the 1971 Census, and delimitation based on the 2011 Census, could persuade the Congress’ current and former allies, particularly the Nationalist Congress Party (Sharadchandra Pawar), which has eight Lok Sabha MPs, and the DMK, which has 22 Lok Sabha MPs. The two parties had helped defeat a similar Bill during the hastily convened special session in mid-April this year. There were also fears in the Opposition camp that several of its MPs could be absent on the day of voting on the Bill.
 
The Congress convened a meeting of its INDIA (Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance) bloc for Saturday morning and invited former ally DMK. Its Parliamentary Strategy Group held a meeting on Friday evening, and the party later alleged that the ultimate objective of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) was the gerrymandering of constituencies, as was done in Assam and Jammu and Kashmir, in the garb of women’s reservation. The party said the BJP has “treated the Election Commission like a puppet”, and a delimitation exercise will follow a similar course.
 
In Chennai, DMK president M K Stalin said that under no circumstances should Tamil Nadu's existing 7.18 per cent share of seats in the Lok Sabha be reduced. He also hit out at the Congress party, which joined the TVK alliance and the government led by it after the DMK was defeated in the Assembly polls held earlier this year. NCP (SP) working president Supriya Sule said she would not attend the INDIA bloc’s meeting on Saturday as her father, Sharad Pawar, was ailing, but another leader said the party would support the Bill.
 
The proposed amendment seeks to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha from the present 543 seats to a maximum of 850 through delimitation. The treasury benches said the move would pave the way for the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in Parliament and state legislative assemblies ahead of the 2029 general election. The fresh Bill seeks to use the 2011 Census to redraw constituencies following the increase in seats. The Cabinet meeting was chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and was convened at 1 pm at Sewa Teerth. The government has called for a four-day special sitting — November 30 and December 1 in the Lok Sabha, and December 2 and 3 in the Rajya Sabha.
 
At a press conference in New Delhi, Independent Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal appealed to Opposition parties to ensure that the delimitation Bill includes a provision that, instead of a single retired judge, there should be a retired judge nominated by the government and another nominated by the Opposition, with both together choosing a third judge to form a three-member delimitation panel. Sibal also highlighted the delay in the case seeking the disqualification of TMC and Shiv Sena (UBT) rebels. Sibal claimed that Parliament would be "defanged", with no debates or transparency. Between April and now, the BJP has used all its might and persuasive power through agencies and other means to persuade some members who are part of the Opposition to agree to this formula, he claimed.
 
(With inputs from Agencies)

data.title: Sebi grants Tata Steel extension till Dec 8 for APL Apollo Tubes open offer
data.description:
The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) on Friday granted Tata Steel an extension until December 8 to publish the detailed statement for its open offer to acquire up to a 26 per cent stake in APL Apollo Tubes, the company said in an exchange filing.
 
The detailed public statement was earlier required to be published by December 1. The extension was granted through an email by Sebi on Friday, following a request submitted by Tata Steel, the filing noted.
 
The extension comes amid concerns raised by proxy advisers, institutional investors, and other shareholders over the deal.
 
However, the deadline for filing the draft letter of offer with Sebi remains unchanged at December 8, 2026, the filing added.
 
 
The company’s management had earlier noted that it would be revising the contours of the deal.

data.title: RBI consolidates card payment rules, reinforces safeguards on tokenisation
data.description:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Friday said that cardholders will have to give explicit consent to link their renewed or replacement cards with merchants with whom they had earlier registered their cards for tokenisation.
 
In its circular, which consolidates 25 circulars, the RBI said that there is a need for explicit customer consent, authenticated through an additional factor of authentication (AFA), for registering cards on token requestor applications. Consent cannot be obtained through pre-selected, default, automatic, or forced options, including checkboxes and radio buttons.
 
It consolidated circulars covering card payments, security measures, tokenisation, card controls, merchant discount rates (MDR), and relaxation of authentication requirements for small-value contactless transactions into a single framework. The directions are effective immediately.
 
 
Under the tokenisation framework, cardholders will be able to register or deregister their cards for specific use cases, such as contactless, QR code-based, and in-app payments. They will also have the facility to set and modify per-transaction and daily limits for tokenised card transactions.
 
Card issuers will have to provide customers with the facility to view merchants with whom their cards have been tokenised and deregister tokens through mobile applications, internet banking, interactive voice response (IVR), or branches. Tokenisation services cannot attract any charges from cardholders.
 
The RBI has also prescribed system and security audits of entities involved in card tokenisation at frequent intervals, at least annually, by auditors empanelled with the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In). Token service providers will have to submit audit reports, details of deviations and compliance, besides monthly data on tokenised transactions, to the central bank.
 
The directions prohibit entities in the card payment chain, other than card issuers and card networks, from storing actual card data for card-not-present transactions. Any such data stored previously will have to be purged. Entities can retain the last four digits of the card number and the issuer's name for transaction tracking and reconciliation.
 
Cards issued or reissued will initially be enabled only for domestic contact-based ATM and point-of-sale (PoS) transactions. Customers will have to activate online, international, and contactless transactions separately, with issuers required to provide round-the-clock controls to switch usage on or off and set transaction limits through mobile applications, internet banking, ATMs, or IVR.
 
The RBI has retained the relaxation of additional authentication requirements for contactless card transactions up to ₹5,000. Beyond this limit, transactions will have to be processed through contact-based payments with authentication. Customers can also choose contact-based payments irrespective of the transaction value.
 
The directions also prescribe debit card MDR caps of 0.40 per cent for small merchants with a turnover of up to ₹20 lakh in the previous financial year and 0.90 per cent for other merchants on physical PoS and online transactions. For QR-based card acceptance, the caps are 0.30 per cent and 0.80 per cent, respectively. The caps are subject to maximum charges of ₹200 per transaction for small merchants and ₹1,000 for other merchants.

data.title: Zee Entertainment buyback to open on Dec 1, set to close on Dec 7
data.description:
Zee Entertainment Enterprises will open its share buyback offer on December 1 and close it on December 7, according to a stock exchange filing by the company on Friday.
 
The company submitted its letter of offer and the tender forms for the proposed buyback to the stock exchanges.
 
Under the buyback, Zee Entertainment plans to buy back up to 65.93 million fully paid-up equity shares with a face value of ₹1 each. The total buyback size is capped at ₹600 crore. The buyback price is ₹91 per share, and the company's share price closed 1.5 per cent higher at ₹67.05 on Friday.
 
 
On November 12, the board of the company approved the buyback.
 
The buyback will be conducted through the tender offer route, allowing eligible shareholders to tender their shares in accordance with the terms set out in the letter of offer.
 
Shareholders wishing to participate in the buyback must submit their completed tender forms and other specified documents to the registrar by December 7, the last date of the offer.
 
The settlement of bids on the stock exchanges is scheduled to be completed by December 14.

data.title: Denmark joins race for Indian tech talent, eyes deeper technology ties
data.description:
Denmark's Minister for Foreign Affairs, Lars Løkke Rasmussen, visited Bengaluru on November 27, 2026, to witness India's impressive tech capabilities and discuss the deepening of technology cooperation between Denmark and India, according to the Embassy of Denmark.
 
While exploring the frontiers of space, quantum technology, and defence in India's premier tech hub, the minister also highlighted the potential for Denmark to attract Indian tech talent, the embassy said.
 
“You have an enormous talent pool with exactly the skills that Danish companies are looking for,” Løkke Rasmussen said.
 
During the visit, the minister launched the report 'Access to Tech Talent in India' by Innovation Centre Denmark in Bengaluru. The report examines the potential for Denmark to attract talent from India. The aim is to meet the domestic challenge of an expanding tech sector with an inadequate supply of skilled labour. The minister acknowledged that Denmark faces competition for those workers.
 
 
“We are not the only ones trying to attract Indian talent,” he said. “So, we also want to make Denmark an attractive place for skilled Indian professionals to go for work.”
 
Denmark has an Innovation Centre at the Consulate General in Bengaluru. The embassy describes the consulate as the only permanent Danish diplomatic representation in India outside New Delhi.
 
“Denmark and Karnataka both understand that innovation is key to our prosperity,” Løkke Rasmussen said. “Our economies thrive on technological advances, and we have much to offer each other. That is why we have partnered with Karnataka and established an Innovation Centre at our consulate here in Bengaluru.”
 
Space, quantum and defence
 
The minister visited C-CAMP, where Denmark's Novo Nordisk Foundation and BioInnovation Institute are present. He also visited quantum company QpiAI. Both visits were to discuss innovation and quantum technology.
 
At the Indian Space Research Organisation (Isro), the minister discussed possible cooperation in space. The talks included how Danish small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and startups can collaborate with Isro.
 
The minister also visited Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd (HAL). Components from the Danish company HBK are being used in the Advanced Light Helicopter and Light Combat Helicopter. They are also used in research and development (R&D) testing of the Tejas fighter jet.
 
He also met Karnataka IT Minister Priyank Kharge and Danish companies present in Karnataka. They discussed the role of global capability centres (GCCs) and India's large tech talent pool.
 
The embassy lists several recent Danish investments in the state.
 
For instance, PowerCurve, a Danish wind turbine blade optimisation company, established its Indian subsidiary in Bengaluru in October 2026.
 
Norican Group expanded its manufacturing operations in Tumakuru with a new greenfield facility in June 2026. The facility produces DISA machines, mould handling systems, and SIMPSON products, strengthening its Indian manufacturing capabilities, according to the embassy.
 
KK Wind Solutions inaugurated its largest manufacturing facility in Asia at Dobbaspet, near Bengaluru, in May 2025. The 17,000 square metre facility produces power converters and control systems for wind turbines, with capacity for up to 400 employees.
 
The visit to Bengaluru will be followed by a visit to New Delhi on Saturday, according to the embassy.

data.title: HSBC India consolidates finance support functions, seeks staff relocation
data.description:
HSBC India is consolidating its finance support functions and has asked employees to relocate to Bengaluru, Gurugram, and Chennai. The London-headquartered lender has asked staff from Kolkata, Hyderabad, and Pune to relocate to those centres. Job losses due to this exercise would be minimal, sources said. HSBC’s India support function has around 48,000 staff.
 
In a statement, an HSBC spokesperson said the changes were part of the bank's efforts to simplify operations and ensure that roles were located where they could best support customers.
 
"As we simplify the bank, our focus remains on ensuring we have the right roles in the right locations to support the best customer outcomes," the spokesperson said.
 
 
The bank is centralising finance support functions in Chennai, Gurugram, and Bengaluru, while phasing out similar roles in other locations. The restructuring is limited to finance functions within the bank's global capability centres (GCCs) in India.
 
HSBC's India GCCs support its global businesses through activities spanning enterprise platforms, analytics and artificial intelligence (AI), risk and controls, and finance and trade operations. Its technology centres also work on automation, data engineering, machine learning, biometrics, and cloud computing, according to the bank's website.
 
According to its annual report, HSBC had 208,720 full-time equivalent employees globally as of December 31, 2025, of whom 47,423 were part of HSBC India. The number of employees in India rose to 48,114 by the end of June 2026.
 
According to a report by Bloomberg, HSBC has been weighing deep job cuts over the coming years as Chief Executive Officer Georges Elhedery deploys AI to shrink its middle and back offices. Non-client-facing roles in global service centres are among those expected to be most affected, people familiar with the matter have said previously. The changes could ultimately affect around 20,000 roles — or about 10 per cent of its total workforce.
 
The consolidation is part of HSBC's broader effort to simplify operations, rationalise costs, and accelerate the adoption of AI, particularly across middle- and back-office functions. The bank has been weighing global workforce reductions of around 20,000 positions over the coming years, or approximately 10 per cent of its workforce, as part of the restructuring, the report said.
 
India has been a key market for HSBC, which emerged as the leading international bank facilitating fundraising by Indian companies through G3 bonds, syndicated loans, and initial public offerings (IPOs) in January-September 2026, leveraging its extensive corporate and institutional relationships and its ability to connect borrowers with pools of capital seeking investment opportunities across debt and equity markets.

data.title: RBI allows white-label ATM operators to buy cash directly from its offices
data.description:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Friday allowed white-label ATM operators to purchase cash directly from its issue offices in wholesale lots, besides sourcing it from banks other than their sponsor banks, in a move that could ease cash replenishment for these operators.
 
In its circular, the RBI said that operators can purchase cash in quantities exceeding one lakh pieces, and in multiples thereof, of any denomination, against full payment. They can also source cash from scheduled commercial banks, cooperative banks, and regional rural banks.
 
The directions, effective immediately, consolidate the existing regulatory framework for white-label ATMs. Operators are required to maintain a minimum net worth of ₹100 crore and ensure ATM deployment is skewed towards semi-urban and rural areas. The minimum deployment ratio across metro, urban, semi-urban, and rural centres is 1:2:3.
 
 
The RBI has also allowed white-label ATM operators (WLAOs) to have multiple sponsor banks and offer interoperable cardless cash withdrawals (ICCW) using the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) for customer authorisation. Settlement of such transactions will be through the National Financial Switch or ATM networks.
 
Withdrawal limits for ICCW transactions will be aligned with those for regular ATM withdrawals. Operators will not be permitted to levy charges beyond the prescribed interchange fee and customer charges.
 
WLAOs can also offer bill payment and interoperable cash deposit services, subject to technical feasibility and certification by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).
 
In a separate circular on cash withdrawals, the RBI retained five free monthly transactions at a bank's own ATMs, including financial and non-financial transactions. At other banks' ATMs, customers will be entitled to three free transactions in metro centres and five in non-metro centres, subject to an overall cap of five if transactions are undertaken across both categories.
 
The maximum cash withdrawal at other banks' ATMs will be ₹10,000 per transaction. Charges beyond the prescribed free transactions will be capped at ₹23 per transaction, plus applicable taxes.
 
Transactions failing due to technical reasons or non-availability of cash will not be counted towards the free transaction limit or attract charges.
 
Cash withdrawals at point-of-sale (PoS) terminals will be permitted through debit cards, full-KYC prepaid payment instruments, and UPI, with a limit of ₹2,000 per transaction and ₹10,000 a month. Charges, if levied, cannot exceed 1 per cent of the transaction amount. The facility will be available even without a purchase. As on end October, there were 2.17 lakh bank managed ATMs and Cash Recycling Machines (CRM) while WTA were 36,000 according to latest RBI data.

data.title: Mini targets over 70% sales growth in India in 2026, eyes 15-20% EV share
data.description:
BMW Group’s British luxury car brand Mini expects its India sales to grow by over 70 per cent in calendar year 2026, driven by the localisation of its petrol-powered Countryman C, network expansion, and new product launches. The company expects electric vehicles (EVs) to initially account for 15-20 per cent of its India sales.
 
Mini on Friday launched its new-generation all-electric Cooper SE at ₹53.9 lakh, along with three special editions developed in collaboration with British fashion designer Sir Paul Smith, priced between ₹55.75 lakh and ₹61.5 lakh (ex-showroom).
 
Having sold around 730 cars last year, Mini could cross 1,240 units in 2026. Its sales grew 70 per cent year-on-year (Y-o-Y) to 504 units in the first half of the calendar year.
  
Hardeep Singh Brar, president and chief executive officer (CEO) of BMW Group India, told Business Standard that Mini could end the year with growth slightly higher than 70 per cent, aided by the availability of new models in December, traditionally a strong month for luxury car sales.
 
Globally, fully electric cars accounted for 37.2 per cent of Mini’s sales of 2.2 lakh units during January-September 2026, according to BMW Group’s quarterly statement. In India, EVs currently account for around 26 per cent of BMW’s sales.
 
“I think it’s too early because we have just announced the prices today. But I think, to begin with, about 15–20 per cent,” Brar said, when asked about the potential share of EVs in Mini’s India sales.
 
While Mini customers have traditionally preferred petrol-powered cars for their driving characteristics, the company is now seeing a shift towards electric vehicles, he said.
 
Local manufacturing of the petrol-powered Countryman C, launched at ₹47.5 lakh earlier this year, has helped drive volumes. The company has no immediate plans to localise its electric models.
 
Brar said the anticipated benefits of the India-United Kingdom (UK) free trade agreement (FTA) had already been factored into the pricing of the relevant UK-sourced models, alongside adverse foreign exchange movements and commodity costs.
 
Mini has also expanded its presence from eight cities last year to around 19 cities, leveraging BMW’s existing dealership infrastructure. While there are no immediate plans for further network expansion next year, the company will evaluate demand from smaller markets.
 
India remains a relatively small market for Mini globally. Brar said the brand had until recently operated with a limited product portfolio in the country and expects a wider model range to drive volumes in the coming years.
 
Around 25-30 per cent of Mini’s customers in India are first-time luxury car buyers, while the majority already own luxury vehicles and buy a Mini as an additional car. Purchases are often occasion-driven, ranging from anniversary and graduation gifts to additions to existing luxury car collections, Brar said.
 
The new electric Cooper SE, imported as a completely built-up unit (CBU), comes with a 54.2 kWh battery offering a range of 402 km under the Worldwide Harmonised Light Vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP), against the 270 km offered by its predecessor. Deliveries will begin immediately.
 
The Paul Smith editions are available across three models — the petrol-powered Cooper S at ₹55.75 lakh, the electric Cooper SE at ₹56.4 lakh, and the Convertible at ₹61.5 lakh. The special editions feature exclusive exterior colours and interior styling inspired by the British designer.

data.title: Adani Group eyes airline investments months after ruling out airline entry
data.description:
The diversified Adani group, which runs multiple airports across the country, has requested the government to allow it to invest in the airline sector, a top official said on Friday.

Group chief finance officer Jugeshinder Robbie Singh told reporters that over 60 crore people in the country can fly, and the number of daily flights needs to go up by nearly 10 times to 30,000.

"And that's why we requested the government to at least allow us to invest, so that we can facilitate the development of airlines. Some fund, some other airline company and things like that...or an entrepreneur who wants to go into that space," the CFO said while speaking on the sidelines of the India Debt Capital Market Summit here.

 

In July this year, the group said it was "not evaluating any proposal to enter the airlines business". On November 3, Adani Airport Holdings chief executive Arun Bansal had ruled out entering the airlines business, saying that it is never a good strategy to compete with customers.

Adani group runs eight airports in the country, including the ones in the financial capital and the satellite city of Navi Mumbai, and also Ahmedabad, Lucknow and Guwahati, which ferry over one-fourth of the country's air passenger traffic.

The airline business has been reduced to a virtual duopoly with two strong domestic carriers -- the Tata Group-led Air India and Rahul Bhatia-run IndiGo, ruling the skies with a 90 per cent market share.

Problems at IndiGo last year, which led to thousands of flight cancellations, led to voices demanding more airlines to operate in the country.
